title: ReplaceArgs documents mutually exclusive and required edit modes but does not validate them
reasoning: The schema exposes three different edit modes: legacy top-level old_string/new_string fields, batched replacements, and patch_chunks. Field descriptions state that new_string is required when old_string is used, replacements override top-level fields, and patch_chunks cannot be combined with old_string/new_string/replacements, but the Pydantic model has no model-level validator enforcing any of those contracts. As a result, invalid or ambiguous payloads such as old_string without new_string, replacements plus patch_chunks, or patch_chunks plus top-level fields can pass schema validation and fail later in execution or be interpreted inconsistently by callers.
recommendation: Add a Pydantic model validator on ReplaceArgs that enforces exactly one edit mode, requires new_string when old_string is provided for legacy mode, rejects patch_chunks combined with replacements or top-level edit fields, and rejects empty replacements or patch_chunks if those are not meaningful operations.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the owned file contains only field-level constraints, so mode-combination validation is currently untested in the shown evidence.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that instantiate ReplaceArgs with valid single-operation, replacements, and patch_chunks payloads, then assert ValidationError for old_string without new_string, patch_chunks combined with replacements, patch_chunks combined with top-level fields, and no edit operation at all.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/tools/filesystem/schemas.py plus focused schema validation tests for ReplaceArgs
